title: Intervalized lease mapping for reserved burst controls
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description:
Problem: Reserved capacity customers see unexpected throttling or credit double-counting near daily/monthly boundaries, DST transitions, and when tenants span multiple reserved pools. Current implementation ties lease tokens to fixed calendar epochs (midnight UTC / monthly boundaries) and performs expensive cross-pool reconciliation during resets, which causes jitter, partial double-debits, and complex rollback logic.

Goal: Replace epoch-bound quota semantics for reserved burst allowances with an intervalized lease mapping that 1) deterministically maps active leases to contiguous interval slices (configurable granularity: 1h/15m/1m), 2) allows lightweight fanout/merge across pools without global epoch coordination, and 3) provides an idempotent reset/rollforward protocol compatible with late-arriving usage events and timezone shifts. The solution must preserve billing accuracy, conserve reserved credits in tension scenarios (cross-tenant borrowing), and reduce reconciliation latencies on cutovers and migrations.
background:
- We've had multiple incidents where overlapping quota resets during migrations caused short overcharging or transient throttles (see INC-2026-47).
- Current epoch approach requires global cutover points which don't map well to reserved pool split/merge operations or to customers that purchased fractional monthly commitments mid-cycle.
- DST and leap-second edge-cases trigger manual reconciliation work and billing adjustments for a small but high-value set of customers.
- Related tickets exist but focus on smoothing resets or proration; this ticket proposes a structural change to core lease bookkeeping to avoid epoch alignment problems.
proposed_solution:
High-level approach: Implement an intervalized lease ledger where each reserved allocation is represented as a set of non-overlapping interval segments [start_ts, end_ts, capacity_units]. Key points: 1) Segments are created at reservation time or on-demand when bursts occur; 2) When a tenant switches pools or we perform a reserved migration, we translate segments by slicing/merging rather than attempting to atomically shift a calendar epoch; 3) Reset semantics become 'expire intervals older than window' instead of 'reset at epoch boundary'; 4) Charge application is idempotent by making usage records reference a unique segment-id + offset; 5) A lightweight compaction pass merges adjacent same-capacity segments to bound growth.

Architecture changes needed: new interval-store (append-only, time-indexed), segment translator service for cross-pool fanout, and modifications to token-draw path to accept segment-scoped reservations. We will maintain a compat layer that maps existing epoch-based queries to intervals to avoid wholesale client changes.
design_decisions: Use configurable interval granularity per-customer (default 15m) to balance resolution vs storage growth
Keep interval store append-only with periodic compaction to avoid in-place mutable state
Record usage as (segment_id, offset, token_count) for deterministic reconciliation
When translating between pools, prefer non-blocking slice+link (creates mirror segments) instead of immediate transfer to avoid cross-region locks
Fallback: if a segment translator fails, route to shared burst pool with tight telemetry and charge attribution markers
acceptance_criteria: 1) No regression for unit tests that assert per-tenant monthly reservation totals; all existing quota invariants preserved
2) Migration path demonstrated: simulate a tenant pool split and show no temporary double-debit or lost credits in 10k request synthetic workload
3) DST/leap-second scenarios have deterministic outcomes — create automated replay tests for two customers in different timezones and assert ledger parity after replay
4) End-to-end latency impact on token-draw path < 2ms median and <5ms p95 after optimization
5) Compaction keeps per-tenant segment count growth < 1% per day for steady workloads (benchmarked)
6) Billing export (CSV/ledger) matches pre-migration totals within 0.001% for randomized test runs
implementation_notes: Phase 1: Interval store prototype as a new Cassandra table keyed by tenant_id + interval_bucket; write path via an append API
Phase 2: Integrate segment_id into token-draw RPC and add translation hook in the request authorizer
Phase 3: Segment translator service deployed in canary region; add metrics and a sanity checker that scans for orphan segments
Phase 4: Compaction worker to merge contiguous segments older than 72 hours with identical capacity footprints
Data migration plan: run a backfill that materializes epoch-era leases into interval segments with a deterministic hash to allow idempotent replay
Backward compatibility: supply a temporary 'epoch-compat' read path for reports relying on calendar boundaries (console/export)
rollout_plan: A) Internal feature flag controls intervalized mode at tenant level; default remains epoch-mode until flag enabled
B) Canary: enable for 5 non-critical reserved tenants, run 48h smoke tests and reconcile ledgers against epoch-mode
C) Gradual ramp: open to additional reserved tenants in waves (10 -> 50 -> 200) with automated reconciliation checks at each wave
D) Full cutover requires final backfill completed and a 6-hour watch window where we compare streaming usage tallies between both modes
E) If discrepancy > threshold, auto-rollback feature flag for affected tenants and trigger triage playbook
test_plan: Unit tests for segment creation, slicing, merging, and idempotent usage application
Integration tests simulating cross-pool migrations with 100k events replayed deterministically
Chaos tests: inject delayed usage events and validate rollforward converges to same billed totals
Performance tests to measure token-draw latency and compaction impact; include p99 SLA verification
End-to-end billing export comparison test that runs nightly during canary waves
telemetry_and_alerts: Alerts: translator_fail_rate > 0.5% over 5m, compaction_backlog > 100k segments, reconciliation_mismatch_rate > 0.01%
Dashboards: per-tenant reconciliation delta, cross-pool embed of 'expected vs actual credits'
Audit logs: every cross-pool translation emits an audit event with original_segment_id -> mirror_segment_id mapping
